profile.campus: Vantage San Antonio Campus (Texas Research Park)
profile.reading:
This building, mapped in this registry as "Vantage TX12" at a separate way ID, is located at 17420 Omicron Drive in the Texas Research Park area of San Antonio, TX; this appears to be another OSM point for the same TX12 building tracked elsewhere in this registry, rather than a distinct facility. Vantage does not publish this campus on its own site at all, so this entry relies on secondary sourcing: Data Center Dynamics reporting on the building permit. TX12 was filed for permit in October 2025 at a stated construction cost of roughly $276.8 million, covering approximately 432,800 square feet across two stories with up to 96 megawatts of power, with a construction timeline running from October 2025 to August 2027.

Vantage acquired 57.9 acres on Omicron/Theta Drive from the University of Texas System Board of Regents in July 2023, and a separate 31 acres at State Highway 151/Wiseman Boulevard in August 2023, forming two San Antonio sub-campuses: Texas Research Park (Omicron Drive, home to TX11 and TX12) and Westover Hills (Rogers Road/Wiseman Boulevard, home to TX21 and TX22). This San Antonio campus is distinct from Vantage's much larger "Frontier" mega-campus, a separate $25 billion, 1.4-gigawatt, 3.7-million-square-foot, 1,200-acre development in rural Shackelford County, Texas, announced in August 2025 to meet AI demand.

San Antonio's data center growth, including Vantage's TX cluster, has concentrated on the city's West and Northwest sides where CPS Energy, the nation's largest municipally owned combined electric and gas utility, has courted large industrial and data center loads with dedicated substations and negotiated rate agreements. Bexar County and the City of San Antonio have both offered property-tax abatement agreements to data center developers as part of a broader economic-diversification push beyond the city's traditional military and tourism base. This OSM point duplicates another mapped point for the same TX12 building elsewhere in this dataset; both are retained here since each corresponds to a distinct upstream map feature, but they should be understood as referring to one physical Vantage building rather than two separate facilities. CPS Energy's integrated resource plan and ERCOT have both cited data centers as a fast-growing large-load category driving new transmission and generation investment across San Antonio through the early 2030s.

reading.body:
Vantage TX12 in San Antonio is planned to deliver 96 MW of critical IT load by August 2027, but remains under construction and not yet operational as of September 2026.

The facility sits within Vantage's Texas Research Park campus in Bexar County, a separate project from the operator's much larger Frontier mega-campus announced for Shackelford County. TX12 represents incremental capacity expansion rather than the scale shift that Frontier signals. At 432,800 square feet and a reported investment of 276.8 million dollars, TX12 is a conventional regional data center deployment, not the gigawatt-scale infrastructure that marks the current frontier of AI compute buildout.

The planned completion date of August 2027 places this facility over a year beyond the research snapshot of September 2026. This timeline matters because it means the 96 MW capacity does not yet contribute to available compute supply. Texas has emerged as a primary hub for data center development, and facilities like TX12 add to that footprint, but their value to AI scaling depends entirely on whether they complete on schedule and whether power infrastructure can support them once they do.

The data does not specify power sourcing, grid connection capacity, or current operational status. It reflects the filed plan, not confirmed reality. Duplicate mapping in OpenStreetMap suggests some uncertainty about the facility's boundaries or whether multiple structures occupy the same address, a minor flag on data quality at the source level.
